title: System design checklist for 0-2 yr engineers
author: Nishant Verma

title: SYSTEM DESIGN
CHECKLIST
pages.takeaway: Name the constraints before the technology.

pages.label: step 1  ·  before you draw anything
title: REQUIREMENTS FIRST
body: Write the numbers down before choosing
any tool. 'Fast' is not a requirement.

pages.label: step 2  ·  the eight numbers
title: NAME THESE EIGHT
body: 3.  data size now, and in a year
pages.takeaway: A design without numbers is a guess.

pages.label: step 3  ·  data layer
title: DATA BEFORE CODE
body: What are the access patterns, not just
Which queries run hottest, and which
Where does the data live for compliance?
pages.takeaway: Schema follows queries, never the reverse.

pages.label: step 4  ·  caching
title: CACHE WITH INTENT
body: What exactly are you caching, and why?
Where: client, CDN, app, or database?
How does it invalidate? What is the TTL?
What happens on a cold start or a
A cache you cannot invalidate is a bug.
pages.takeaway: Invalidation is the design, caching is the trick.

pages.label: step 5  ·  scale
title: READS AND WRITES
body: Always ask: what is the sharding key,
and what makes it a hot partition?
pages.takeaway: The key choice decides the ceiling.

pages.label: step 6  ·  async work
title: QUEUES AND RETRIES
body: What work leaves the request path?
Dead letter queue, and who watches it?
Does ordering matter, and for what?

pages.label: step 7  ·  failure
title: DESIGN FOR BREAKAGE
body: Blast radius of one bad deploy?

pages.label: step 8  ·  observability
title: YOU CANNOT FIX
WHAT YOU CANNOT SEE
body: Logs with request IDs. Traces across services.
An SLO with an error budget.
Alert on symptoms users feel, not causes.
pages.takeaway: p99 is the user experience, not the average.

pages.label: step 9  ·  security and cost
title: THE TWO QUIET ONES
body: Auth: who can do what, and where is that
PII: what is stored, and for how long?
Rate limits, and cost per request.
pages.takeaway: Both are design inputs, not afterthoughts.

pages.label: step 10  ·  the review
title: THREE QUESTIONS
THAT END REVIEWS
body: 1.  What breaks first when load doubles?
2.  How do we roll this back in ten minutes?
pages.takeaway: If you cannot answer, the design is not done.

pages.label: the point
title: TRADE-OFFS,
NOT TOOLS
body: Nobody is asking whether you know Kafka.
They are asking whether you know why
you chose it, and what it costs you.
Design is the set of trade-offs you can
defend - not the list of things you used.
pages.takeaway: Defend the choice, not the logo.
